title: CPT Code 45378: Diagnostic Colonoscopy Billing and Coding Explained (2026)
summary: A comprehensive guide to billing diagnostic colonoscopy procedures using CPT 45378 with proper modifiers and documentation guidelines.

content.introduction: CPT code 45378 is used to report a diagnostic colonoscopy, flexible, with or without collection of specimen(s) by brushing or washing, when performed without additional interventions.

sections.heading: Key Coding Guidelines
sections.body: Ensure the medical record clearly documents the reason for the procedure (e.g., GI bleeding, abnormal imaging, or surveillance). If a polyp or lesion is excised, appropriate operative codes must be selected instead.

sections.heading: Modifier Applications
sections.body: Common modifiers used include Modifier 33 for preventive services or Modifier 53 if the procedure is discontinued due to inadequate bowel preparation.

content.conclusion: Accurate modifier selection and pre-authorization verification remain the key steps to preventing claim rejections for CPT 45378.

title: CPT Code 29827: Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair Billing Explained
summary: Step-by-step coding and billing instructions for arthroscopic rotator cuff repairs and associated bundled procedures.

content.introduction: CPT code 29827 covers surgical arthroscopy of the shoulder with rotator cuff repair.

sections.heading: CCI Edit Bundling Rules
sections.body: Be mindful of NCCI edits when coding subacromial decompression (29826) or distal clavicle resection (29824) alongside CPT 29827.

content.conclusion: Detailed operative reports that specify the exact tendons repaired ensure maximum compliant reimbursement.

title: Proven AR Recovery Strategies for Aging Accounts Receivable in 2026
summary: Actionable tactics to recover aged receivables, reduce days in AR, and improve cash flow for medical practices and ASCs.

sections.heading: Prioritizing High-Value Claims
sections.body: Segment aging reports by payer, balance, and denial reason so recovery efforts focus first on the highest-dollar opportunities.

sections.heading: Effective Follow-Up and Appeal Workflows
sections.body: Structured follow-up cadence combined with strong appeal letter templates and secondary insurance billing can recover a substantial portion of aged balances.

content.conclusion: Consistent AR recovery processes typically reduce days in A/R by 15–25 days within the first six months.
